description:
`World::demand_function_scope` (src/compiler2/world.rs:2709-2744) diagnoses a
duplicate `name/arity` only when `module.is_global()`. The non-global branch has
NO equivalent check:

    if self.module_has_source_state(module) || self.ensure_runtime_module(module).is_some() {
        return Ok(vec![FactKey::ModuleDefined(module)]);
    }

Nothing in source_publish.rs or world.rs diagnoses a module-scoped `name/arity`
collision either; the only module-level duplicate check is
`duplicate_struct_diagnostic` for `defstruct` (source_publish.rs:968).

## User-visible today

    defmodule List do
      fn count(_list), do: 999
    end

    fn main() do
      dbg(List.count([7, 8]))
    end

prints `999`, exit 0, NO diagnostic -- the user's `count/1` silently displaces
the runtime library's. Add `dbg(List.member?([7, 8], 8))` to the same file and
you get:

    error[resolve/unknown-import]: module `List` does not export `member?/2`

The collision replaced the WHOLE runtime module surface, and the only signal the
user gets is a confusing downstream error about an unrelated function.

ELIXIR's answer for a cross-file module collision is
`warning: redefining module Foo (current version defined in memory)` plus
last-definition-wins -- a warning, not silence.

## What the old ticket got wrong -- its title case is NOT a defect

"Two `def foo` inside `defmodule`" is fz's normal MULTI-CLAUSE form. `fz2`
returns the first clause's answer (2), exactly as Elixir does. (Elixir
additionally warns `this clause for bar/1 cannot match because a previous clause
always matches` -- a separate, smaller gap worth its own ticket if wanted.)

The real gap, matching the parent's framing, is TWO CODES. The global check
covers two separate codes, never two clauses in one file, so "only global-module
top-level is covered" mis-describes what it covers.

Line cite drifted: world.rs:2343-2346 -> world.rs:2740-2743.

## Not fully verified

A genuine two-code module-scoped `name/arity` duplicate could not be constructed
through the CLI, because the fz2 front door submits exactly one code. The
`List.count/1` repro proves A silent module-scoped collision with no diagnostic,
but it is module REPLACEMENT (the runtime List surface disappears), not
necessarily two indexed codes contending for one FunctionId. Settling that needs
a unit test with two `submit_code` calls, mirroring drive_test.rs:1170.

## Checks

- A unit test mirroring drive_test.rs:1170 but with the duplicate inside a
  `defmodule` -- two `submit_code` calls, each `defmodule Foo do fn bar(), do: N
  end` -- produces a `RESOLVE_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION` diagnostic naming `Foo.bar/0`
  and its second span, instead of silently resolving.
- The `defmodule List` repro either diagnoses the collision or is documented as
  intentional shadowing; either way `List.member?/2` must not disappear without a
  signal.
- The global-duplicate test and the defstruct duplicate test stay green.
title: A module-scoped function definition can be silently replaced across codes; the duplicate check exists only on the global branch
